brief: Goldman's mid-day US equities color for Oct 23 frames today's session as reversion from yesterday's violent de-grossing event: GS calls 10/22 the 5th largest de-grossing event of the year at -1.6 standard deviations, driven entirely by long selling (the largest since September 2025) across 9 of 11 sectors, with info tech seeing the largest net selling since September 2024 from both long selling and short additions. Today the momentum pair, the HF positioning pair, the AI basket and the Nasdaq-100 are all bouncing off yesterday's losses, but breadth is deteriorating (over 70% of the S&P 500 is in the red) and Brent crude is surging above $117/bbl on Middle East tensions. The desk's own franchise flows, long-onlys and hedge funds all remain net sellers today. Looking ahead, GS flags CTAs as projected sellers in every tape scenario next week, against a backdrop of heavy event risk: 44% of the S&P reports earnings, including GOOGL, MSFT and AMZN, alongside the Fed's rate decision on Wednesday.
